record.paper_title: The Critical Beta-splitting Random Tree II: Overview and Open Problems
record.original_question: Study the full distributional behavior, not just expectations, of balance indices for DTCS(n), including the examples discussed in the paper such as the Colless index, quadratic Colless index, B1, B2, ŝ-shape index, total cophenetic index, variance of leaf heights, and rooted quartet index, as well as other balance indices on the same model.

evidence.quote: A longstanding topic in mathematical and statistical phylogenetics concerns tree balance indices, that is statistics which measure “balance” of a given tree in some quantitative way.
Open Problem 10 Study the distribution of these and other indices for DTCS(n) in more detail.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Define the critical beta-splitting random tree model DTCS(n) as follows. For each integer m ≥ 2, let q(m, i) for 1 ≤ i ≤ m−1 be the probability distribution
  q(m, i) = (1/h_{m-1}) · (1/(i(m−i))) · (m choose ... ) 
more precisely, the critical (β = −1) split distribution
  q(m, i) = (m / (2 h_{m-1})) · 1/(i (m − i)),   1 ≤ i ≤ m − 1,
where h_{m-1} = 1 + 1/2 + ⋯ + 1/(m−1). The random rooted binary tree DTCS(n) with n labeled leaves is constructed recursively: starting from the root labeled with the set [n] = {1,…,n}, a node labeled with a set S of size m ≥ 2 is split into two children labeled with a uniformly random partition of S into a part of size I and a part of size m − I, where I has distribution q(m, ·); the recursion stops at singleton leaves.

For a rooted binary tree T with n leaves, define the following balance indices:

(1) Colless index: C(T) = Σ_v |L(v) − R(v)|, summed over internal nodes v, where L(v), R(v) are the numbers of leaves in the two subtrees rooted at the children of v.
(2) Quadratic Colless index: C_q(T) = Σ_v (L(v) − R(v))².
(3) B1 index: B1(T) = Σ_{v internal, v ≠ root} 1/M(v), where M(v) is the maximum number of edges between v and any leaf descendant of v.
(4) B2 index: B2(T) = − Σ_{ℓ leaf} p_ℓ log p_ℓ, where p_ℓ = 2^{−d(ℓ)} with d(ℓ) the depth of leaf ℓ in the corresponding equiprobable random walk from the root.
(5) ŝ-shape index: ŝ(T) = Σ_v log(n(v) − 1), where n(v) is the number of leaves in the subtree rooted at v.
(6) Total cophenetic index: Φ(T) = Σ_{i < j} depth(lca(i, j)), summed over unordered pairs of leaves.
(7) Variance of leaf heights: σ²(T) = (1/n) Σ_ℓ d(ℓ)² − ((1/n) Σ_ℓ d(ℓ))².
(8) Rooted quartet index: the sum, over 4-element subsets {i,j,k,ℓ} of leaves, of weights assigned to the seven possible rooted quartet topologies induced on {i,j,k,ℓ}.

For each of these balance indices X = X_n evaluated on T = DTCS(n), determine the full asymptotic distributional behavior (beyond merely its expectation) as n → ∞: identify centering and scaling sequences a_n, b_n and a non-degenerate limit law L such that (X_n − a_n)/b_n ⇒ L, and characterize L (for example via its moments, Laplace transform, or as the fixed point of a distributional recursion). Carry out the analogous analysis for other natural balance indices defined on rooted trees applied to DTCS(n).
artifact.status_search_result: The critical beta-splitting (β = −1) DTCS model is the subject of recent work by Aldous and Pittel, who established expectations and Gaussian-type limits for some statistics (e.g. height of a uniform random leaf). However, full distributional limits for the listed balance indices (Colless, quadratic Colless, B1, B2, ŝ-shape, total cophenetic, leaf-height variance, rooted quartet index) on DTCS(n) have not been established in the literature found. Distributional results exist for Aldous's β ≥ 0 model (e.g. the quartet balance index), but not for the critical β = −1 case in the requested generality, so the problem appears open.

status_evidence.title: The Critical Beta-Splitting Random Tree Model: Results and Open Problems (Aldous talk)
status_evidence.snippet: Presents results and open problems for DTCS(n) and CTCS(n), including recursive analysis and Gaussian limits for some statistics; balance index distributions listed as open.
status_evidence.claim: Distributional study of balance indices on DTCS(n) is highlighted as an open direction.

status_evidence.title: Limit distribution of the quartet balance index for Aldous's β ≥ 0-model (arXiv:1803.02136)
status_evidence.snippet: Provides limit distributions for the quartet balance index in the β ≥ 0 regime of Aldous's beta-splitting model.
status_evidence.claim: Distributional results exist for β ≥ 0 but not for the critical β = −1 model in the generality requested.
